newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq condemns U.S. over embassy in Israel - paper.
newsitem.headline: Iraq condemns U.S. over embassy in Israel - paper.

text.p: A senior Iraqi official condemned on Sunday a vote by the U.S. House of Representatives reaffirming an earlier commitment to move the U.S. embassy in Israel to Jerusalem by 1999, and urged Arab countries to sever ties with Washington.

"The transfer of any embassy to Jerusalem is an act of aggression against the Arabs which is unacceptable," former information minister Abdul-al-Ghani Abdul-al-Ghafur said in a commentary published by al-Jumhouriya newspaper.

Ghafur, who is a senior member of the ruling Baath party, said Arab rulers should stick to a decision taken by the Arab summit held in Amman in 1980 which urged Arab countries to "sever all ties with any state which recognises Jerusalem as capital for Israel or moves its embassy to it."

"Adopting such decision exposes policies of America which was and is still keen to achieve the will and policy of the Zionist enemy," he said. "Nobody can claim that such an American decision does not pose a threat to the Arab homeland."
Ghafur also criticised Arab leaders' reaction to the House resolution, saying they had only voiced "weak statements."
Iraq, which fired scores of Scud missiles on the Jewish state during the 1991 Gulf War over Kuwait, is still theoretically at war with Israel.
Its official media carried reports opposing the making of peace by Arabs with Israel. Baghdad has also denied Western reports of clandestine contacts with Tel Aviv.
